# held/ — every output the repo owner must review or act on, held in a file at the moment it is emitted

This directory is a store of the fleet's held output: everything a session shows the repo owner that he has
to review, decide, unblock or give input on. A `/format-decision` + `/explain` pair, a blocker, an
`/exit-goal` report, a `/progress-review`, a `/summary`, an `/auto-start` final report, a fleet
brief the chief wrote for him. The session that produces such an output writes it here **before**
it emits it (§ Holding at emit time), so that the exact text can be shown to him again, in full, if
newer work buries it in the transcript before he has reviewed and answered all of it; the chief and
other sessions see only its path and its one-line `ask`.

the repo owner, 2026-10-11 (the founding ask, `docs/asks/(internal ref)`):
"for any output that i need to review and unblock or make decisions or provide input on, you and/or
those cc sessions should be writing that output to 'held' doc files and shipping those changes as
appropriate via /sync-git". the repo owner, 2026-10-11, to kg-3 (`(internal ref)`): "you should always be
writing the fully /exit-goal or any /format-decision / /explain or /progress-review etc (anything
that you post in your cc session trasncript as output that needs my review and input etc) message a
held file so you can redisplay it in the cc session output later if it ends up getting buried".
The core (layout, schema, lifecycle, CLI):
[📄 ai-harness/docs/plans/aih-mi8lo-chief-of-staff-fleet-coordination-plan.md](../plans/aih-mi8lo-chief-of-staff-fleet-coordination-plan.md)
(D-4 layout, D-5 lifecycle, D-7 shipping, D-11 routing, D-12 the session address). The extension
(emit-time holding, replay, per-repo stores as the owner ruled them, the decision-record rule):
[📄 ai-harness/docs/plans/aih-ejk7o-hold-every-review-output-plan.md](../plans/aih-ejk7o-hold-every-review-output-plan.md)
(D-1 to D-12). Where the two plans disagreed, the extension's D-1 and D-4 govern, under the later
ask; this README is the one place the resulting convention is stated in full.

## The one question: does the repo owner have to review, answer or give input on this?

- **Yes** (every output in the table under § Holding at emit time) → it is a held item: write it
  with `held_cli.py add` before you emit it, emit the same text, ship on the cadence below, and put
  `Held: <absolute path>` under it in chat.
- **No** (a log, a tool's stdout, an intermediate reading, an output he has already answered) → it
  is not a held item.

A request to approve a design or plan doc whose every Decision is decided and every Open Question
resolved is a **No**: a fully decided doc is approved, so the session builds it instead of holding
it. It is a **Yes** only when he explicitly asked to review that doc
(`docs/procedures/decision-framework.md` § A fully decided doc is approved).

There is one store system and no second one. A session that cannot reach `held_cli.py` at the
moment it emits (no ai-harness checkout on the machine; a denied command) says so in chat and in
its resume message's `STATUS`, and holds the output at the next window that can
(§ Holding at emit time, the repair route).

## Holding at emit time

**The producer rule (plan (internal ref) D-3: file first, then emit).** The session writes the finished
output to a staging file, `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/.held-body-<session slug>-<UTC stamp>.md`,
with the `Write` tool, runs `held_cli.py toc <that file>` when the output holds a decision
(§ Decision headings and the approved marker), runs `held_cli.py add --body-file <that file> ...`,
and then emits **that same text** in chat followed by one line, `Held: <the absolute path add printed>`. The staging file is
deleted once `add` has printed the path. The file is the source and the chat the copy: do not
compose a second version for chat, and never re-type an output into a file after showing it. The
body `add` keeps is byte for byte.

**Who holds.** The session that produced the output. A sub-agent never holds for the repo owner itself: it
reports to its launcher, which decides what he must see and holds it (§ Who writes here). Where one
skill composes another's output (`/summary` § 2 composes `/progress-review`; `/exit-goal` composes
`/summary`, `/progress-review` and each `/format-decision` + `/explain` pair), the inner skill's own
step holds the inner output and the composing skill holds only what it adds.

**Session identity (D-7).** Every verb takes `--session <slug>@<host>`, the fleet's one session
address ((internal ref)). Derive it as `${CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID}@${AI_HOST}`; never guess a slug. A
session with no `CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID` names its slug from its `ai` launch name and says so.
On disk the session's directory, its landing pad and its aggregate held review doc use the board form
`<host>--<slug>` (§ Layout); the address never changes with the store an item lands in.

**What each producer holds (D-8).** The seven `kind` values are the core's; `source_skill` tells
producers of the same kind apart.

| Producer | `kind` | `title` | default `ask` | `task` | `source_skill` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/format-decision` + `/explain` (one item whose body is both outputs in order) | `decision` | the decision's name (`D-N: ...` when in a doc) | the Recommendation's one-line question | the orientation block's Beads id | `/format-decision <args>[, then /explain]` |
| `/explain`, standalone | `other` | `explain: <target>` | "Confirm this answers your question, or name the next depth" | the target's Beads id or `none` | `/explain <target>` |
| `/progress-review` | `progress-review` | `progress review <date> <session slug>` | "Review the briefing; reply to any item to change or re-prioritise it" | `none` | `/progress-review` |
| `/summary` | `summary` | `summary: <batch scope>` | "Review the retrospective; reply with corrections or next-step changes" | the batch's epic or `none` | `/summary <scope>` |
| `/auto-start` Step 4 final report | `summary` | `auto-start report <date> <session slug>` | "Review the autonomous run: the review queue needs your answers" | `none` | `/auto-start Step 4` |
| `/exit-goal` Step 6 index | `exit-goal` | `exit-goal <date> <session slug>` | "Review the exit report; answer each open decision it indexes" | the goal's epic or `none` | `/exit-goal` |
| a blocker surfaced mid-run | `blocker` | the blocker in one line | what unblocks it | the blocked Beads id | the skill, or `report` |
| a large ad-hoc report | `other` | `report: <topic>` | the report's own ask | its Beads id or `none` | `report: <topic>` |
| the chief's fleet brief | `fleet-brief` | the brief's title | the brief's ask | `none` | `/fleet-brief` |

**Ship cadence (D-2).** `add` runs at emit time, always. `ship --session <id>` runs immediately
after an `add` of kind `decision`, `blocker` or `exit-goal` (the repo owner or the chief must act on it); at
`/save-state` Step 0.7 for everything else; at `/exit-goal` Step 6; and before any message that
hands another session or machine a `docs/held/` path. One `ship` call covers every store that holds
an unshipped item of the session. A locally committed item is already durable across compaction and
reboot; between `add` and `ship` it is visible to its own session (the hook and `/auto-start` read
the landing pads through `list`) and not yet to the chief's `fleet` view.

**Not held is a defect, not a choice.** An output shown to the repo owner without an `add` is repaired
before any other work with `scripts/held_capture_last_output.py` (it writes the session's last
emitted assistant text to a file, byte for byte, from the transcript; `--anchor` selects an earlier
message by its first line), then `add --body-file` on that file (with `--unchecked` for a
`decision`: the text was already shown, so a failing `/format-decision` check is printed, not
refused); the omission is noted in the resume
message's `STATUS`. Never re-type the output.

## Where an item lives

**The store is not chosen by the session.** `add` resolves it from
`config/agent_artifact_routing.toml` (`[[held_routes]]`) by this machine and by the repository the
session is working in (`--source-repo`, default the current checkout's registered name, stated on
stderr), and prints the absolute path it wrote; that path is what the session records, and it is
how a `bms-semantic-knowledge-graph` session's item is found in `sw-bms-workspace` later. Run `add`
from the checkout you are working in, by the absolute invocation in § Writing, shipping, listing. A session that wants a different store changes the table
through aih-firstmate-1 (the core's owner), never the command: no skill, hook or procedure passes,
computes or hard-codes a store path.

The table expresses the repo owner's ruling of 2026-10-12 (plan (internal ref) D-1, verbatim there): the store
is configurable per repo and per machine profile; **a personal repo's items go to
`ai-harness/docs/held/` on every machine; a `bms-semantic-knowledge-graph` session's go to
`sw-bms-workspace/docs/held/`.** A route names a repository by its registered name under the
projects directory (`config/fleet-projects.toml`), never an absolute path; rows are keyed on the
machine (`AI_HOST`, or `"*"` for every machine) and on `source_repo`, the repo the held work belongs
to and never the session's name or prefix; the first matching row in file order wins. The shipped
rows: `bms-semantic-knowledge-graph` and `sw-bms-workspace` itself → `sw-bms-workspace/docs/held`
(`land = "push"`; the second keeps a session working from the workspace repo in one store,
(internal ref)), and
`source_repo = "*"` → `ai-harness/docs/held` (`land = "pr"`), where the `"*"` row matches only a
source whose checkout origin is not `bms-corp/*`; a `bms-corp` source with no explicit row refuses
naming the table, so (employer ref) content never lands in a personal repo by default, and a `bms-corp/*`
repository is never a destination. That table is the only place a destination is declared.

Why the second store exists: a held body is chat output and carries internal dev-tracking ids
(`AIH-`, `KG-`, `SW-`, `D-N`), which must never land in a `bms-corp` repo. `sw-bms-workspace` is
the repo owner's own single-author repository (`sergeiwallace-bms/sw-bms-workspace`, not `bms-corp`), so its
held files carry no (employer ref) publication gate, and the no-internal-ids rule applies to
`bms-semantic-knowledge-graph` content, not to a held body stored there. It lands by `push` (a
fast-forward of the pad branch onto `main`, no forge call) because no `gh` identity on sem-kg-ec2
resolves that repository (measured 2026-10-12). `sw-bms-workspace/docs/held/README.md` is a
one-paragraph pointer back to this file; the convention is defined here only.

A session that works in two repositories holds into two stores (kg-3 holds into `sw-bms-workspace`
from its (employer ref) checkout and into ai-harness from an ai-harness worktree); its items are one queue
split by routing, which is why every reader below looks in every store (D-10).

## Layout

```text
docs/held/
  README.md                                   # this file; never an item
  <machine>--<slug>/                          # one directory per session: the board form of its address
    <YYYY-MM-DD>-<NN>-<kind>-<topic>.md       # NN: per-session, per-day sequence from 01
  <machine>--<slug>-held-review.md            # reserved: the aggregate held review doc, never an item ((internal ref) D-2)
  <machine>--<slug>-open-decisions.md         # reserved: the legacy decisions-only digest it replaced; compile removes it
```

A session is addressed as `<slug>@<host>` (`aih-3@sem-kg-ec2`, `aih-bootstrap-1@acn-mac`; the repo owner's
2026-10-11 ruling, (internal ref), the fleet's `vp_id`): that is what the `session` key and every
`--session` carry. On disk the directory and the landing-pad worktree use its board form
`<host>--<slug>` (`sem-kg-ec2--aih-3`), the same crossing the Agent Mail board uses, converted by
`session_address.board_name` (plan D-12); `chief_of_staff_cli.py inventory` lists the addresses.
`<kind>` and `<topic>` are lowercase hyphenated slugs. Example:
`docs/held/sem-kg-ec2--aih-2/2026-10-11-01-decision-xhc5u-d6-upgrade-claude-code.md`.

## File format

Frontmatter carries exactly these keys; the body is the originating skill's output **verbatim**,
followed by a `## Answer` heading that is empty until the repo owner answers. Verbatim includes trailing
spaces, so every store exempts `docs/held/` from the `trailing-whitespace` hook and turns
markdownlint's MD009 off in `docs/held/.markdownlint.yaml`; either one rewriting a body line
refused the verb's own commit ((internal ref)).

```yaml
---
held_schema: 1
kind: decision            # decision | blocker | exit-goal | progress-review | summary | fleet-brief | other
status: open              # open | answered
session: aih-2@sem-kg-ec2
machine: sem-kg-ec2
task: (internal ref)           # a Beads id (display or hash), or none
title: "D-6: upgrade Claude Code on the sem-kg pair"
ask: "Approve (a) upgrade now, or pick (b)/(c); one word is enough."
source_skill: "/format-decision (internal ref) D-6, then /explain"
created_at: 2026-10-11T23:05:12Z
answered_at: null
answer_recorded_in: null  # a bd comment ref or a doc path#anchor; set by `answer --recorded-in`, else named in the retiring commit
---

<the skill output, byte for byte>

## Answer

```

An item written by `/escalate-decision` also carries `decider`, `escalation_id`, `recommended`,
`chosen`, `decider_model` and `escalated_to_sergei` ((internal ref)). Such an item is addressed to the
decider session named in `decider`, not to the repo owner, and its answer is the decider's ruling. Compile
and replay list it under "Escalated to a decider", never among the repo owner's open decisions, unless
`escalated_to_sergei` is true. Design: `docs/designs/aih-2zmvc-decision-escalation-routing.md`.

`kind` tells the reader what shape to expect; `ask` is the one line the repo owner reads first and is what
the chat and `/fleet-brief` print beside the path. Keep it to one sentence that names the action.

## Links

Every held body links each file, doc and URL it names, so the repo owner opens it with one click in the
VS Code editor on the host and on GitHub. Every held README, rule, skill, procedure, STUB.md and
TEMPLATE.md carries these two sentences byte for byte (a TEMPLATE inside an HTML comment, so they
never render into a body):

```text
Canonical first: read the ai-harness version of the held README, of each kind's STUB.md and TEMPLATE.md and of every other held doc (~/projects/ai-harness/docs/held/ and ~/projects/ai-harness/docs/prompts/held/) before any repository-specific copy, and use a repository-specific version only for what it adds or changes.
Links: write every file or doc a held body references as a Markdown link with display text, [📄 <repo>/<path>](<path relative to the item's directory>), and every URL (a Jira issue, a Confluence page, a pull request, anything else) as [<display text>](<URL>), never a bare path or URL; held_cli.py link prints the file form and held_cli.py add refuses a bare one (docs/held/README.md § Links).
```

the repo owner, 2026-10-20 (the founding ask,
[📄 ai-harness/docs/asks/(internal ref)](../asks/(internal ref))):
"you need to add backlinks to any and all other docs or files that are referenced in any held doc
file ... you always need to add URL hyperlinks with display text so i can click to open them."
The plan, with the decisions behind each form below:
[📄 ai-harness/docs/plans/aih-held-docs-clickable-backlinks-plan.md](../plans/aih-held-docs-clickable-backlinks-plan.md)
(D-1 to D-7). The forms follow the fleet's doc-link convention
([📄 ai-harness/projects-wide-session-config/rules/doc-authoring.md](../../projects-wide-session-config/rules/doc-authoring.md)
§ File-path references & doc links). A link target is relative to the item's directory,
`docs/held/<host>--<slug>/` in its store's main tree, because VS Code resolves a target starting
with `/` against the workspace folder and GitHub against the repository, so an absolute target
opens nothing in either.

| Reference | Form |
|---|---|
| a file in the store's own repository | `[📄 <repo>/<relpath>](../../../<relpath>)` |
| a file in another repository | `[📄 <repo>/<relpath> (local)](../../../../<repo>/<relpath>) ([GitHub](https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/main/<relpath>))` |
| a file outside every repository (a transcript, a log) | `[📄 <absolute path>](<relative path>)`; it opens on the host only |
| a URL | `[<display text>](<URL>)`: a Jira issue `[KEY-123](https://<site>/browse/KEY-123)`, a pull request `[PR #N](https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/N)`, a Confluence page by its title |
| a path-shaped name that is not a file (an S3 key, a CloudWatch log group, an ARN) | its console page as a URL, `[<the name>](<console URL>)`; a generic example path takes a placeholder segment, `<folder>/config.yaml`, so it names no file |
| a decision's three path lines | the absolute path as display text, which chat shows and the terminal opens: `Recorded in: [<abs>#<anchor>](<relative>#<anchor>)`, `Held: [<abs>](<file name>)`, `Compiled in: [<abs>](../<file name>)`; the same for `Old held:` in a case 2 review and each path in an exit-goal's `Held this run:` list |

`held_cli.py link --session <s>@<m> <absolute path>[#anchor]...` prints the link for each file,
computed from the session's routed store; `--absolute` shows the absolute path as the display text
for the path lines, and `add --plan` prints `Held:` and `Compiled in:` already linked. A chat line
outside a body (`Held: <path>` after a non-decision body, `Held for you:`, `Held output
(replayed):`) stays a bare absolute path, because it never lands in a file and the terminal opens
it.

What counts as a reference (plan D-4). Outside fenced code, HTML comments, Markdown links and
images, reference definitions, and inline code that holds whitespace (a command), a token with its
surrounding punctuation stripped is a bare URL when it carries `http://` or `https://`, and a bare
path when it is an absolute or `~/` path of two or more segments, or a relative path whose last
segment has a file extension (`#anchor` and `:line` ignored). A token holding `<`, `>`, `{`, `}`,
`*`, `$`, `|`, `=` or an ellipsis is a placeholder and is skipped. A path in backticks with no
whitespace is still a bare path. A Jira key named alone is not detected, because it reads the same
as a tracking id; link it anyway.

Enforcement (plan D-3, D-7). `add` refuses (exit 4, nothing written) a body of any kind with a bare
reference and prints one `<file>:<line>: HL-01 bare path <token>. Fix: ...` or `HL-02 bare URL`
line per finding, and under each bare absolute or `~` path the finished link to paste,
`  link: [📄 <repo>/<relpath>](<relative>)`, computed as `link` computes it; `add --unchecked`, the
capture-repair route, holds it and prints the same lines.
`scripts/held_links_check.py check <staging file>` runs the same scan before `add`. The `held-links`
pre-commit hook runs it over every held item file a commit adds, never a modified, renamed or
deleted one, never while a rebase replays commits (`ship`'s ledger-conflict continue), and never on
an item a merge brings unchanged from the branch it merges in, so merging the trunk never refuses
another session's item. An item held before 2026-10-20 is history and keeps its bare paths until it is
superseded; `compile` links every path it prints whatever the body carries.

## Decision headings and the approved marker

Every decision in a held doc has its own heading, linked from the doc's table of contents, and the
heading of an approved decision says so. the repo owner, 2026-10-23, to aih-ec2-firstmate-1 (epic
`(internal ref)`): "all decisions have their own linked header line in the table of contents so i can navigate to
each. also need to mark in the header of each decision when they are approved so i know to skip
it." Both are generated and checked by the tools; nobody types them.

### What counts as a decision

In an item of any kind, each `/format-decision` block, from its
`<!-- format-decision:begin id="<id>" ... -->` line to its end marker, is one decision, keyed by
its `id`. A `decision` item held before the markers existed, with no block, is one decision: the
item itself, keyed by its `task` (else its file stem). In the aggregate held review doc, each
`decision` item it lists is one decision.

### The heading and the table of contents of an item

Directly above each decision's first line:

```markdown
<a id="decision-<id, lowercased, each run of other characters a hyphen>"></a>
## Decision <id>: <label>
```

The label is the item's `title` when a `decision` item holds one decision, else the title of the
other `decision` item the block's `Held:` line names, else the block's bold headline after its display id. The level is one
below the nearest `#` or `##` section above it, so a decision sits at `##` in its own item and at
`###` under a summary's `## Decisions` section. The body opens, after its
`<!-- held:<kind>:begin -->` line and its H1 when it has them, with the generated region:

```markdown
<!-- held-toc:begin -->
## Table of Contents

- [Decision <id>: <label>](#decision-<id slug>)
<!-- held-toc:end -->
```

`held_cli.py toc <file>` writes both into a staged body (`--title` the `add --title`, `--kind`
when it is not a `decision`) in place, or into a held item named by any checkout's path, which it
fixes in the session's landing pad and commits there, like `answer`, so a store's main tree is
never edited ((internal ref)). It is idempotent: a heading it already
wrote keeps its anchor, level and label, so a link to the anchor never breaks. Run it on the
staging file before `add`, then emit the file's text, so the chat copy and the held body stay one
text.

### The aggregate

`compile` writes a `####` heading for every decision it lists: each open one
under `### Decisions, in full`, each escalated one under `### Escalated to a decider`, and each
answered one under `### Answered decisions`, which lists the item's `Held:` link, `answered_at`
and durable record without its body. Each sits under its own anchor
`<a id="held-<item file stem slug>"></a>`, which does not change when the item moves from open to
answered or gains the marker, and the table of contents links every one beside the `##` and `###`
sections. An item that holds several decisions also gets one entry per decision, one level
below its own, linking the decision's heading in the inlined body; when another inlined body
carries the same anchor, the entry links the item's heading instead, so it never lands on a
different body's copy.

### What approved means

A decision is approved when the question has been answered by the one it
was put to. That is the existing lifecycle, never a parallel state:

- a held item is approved once `held_cli.py answer` has moved it to `status: answered`, on the
  date of its `answered_at`, whichever option the answer picked, and whether the answer is
  the repo owner's or, for an item addressed to a decider, that decider's ruling; an item a decider passed
  on to the repo owner stays `open` and is not approved;
- a partial answer (§ Answering, partial answers and supersession) approves the answered part
  only: each decision that the open item named by `--recorded-in` carries forward, a remainder
  or a superseding item, stays open in the original as well;
- in the aggregate, an open decision whose `Recorded in:` record now reads `✅ Approved` (the same
  test `compile` reports under `settled`) is marked too, dated when that record names a date.
  Its held item stays open until its session settles it.

### The marker

An approved decision's heading, and its table of contents entry, end in
` ✅ Approved <YYYY-MM-DD>`, the same `✅ Approved` a governing doc's Decision line uses, or bare
` ✅ Approved` when the record names no date. An open decision carries no marker. `answer` writes
it into the item it answers, changing nothing else above `## Answer`, so `ship`'s answer-only
exemption (§ Answering) still applies; `compile` writes it into the aggregate.

### The check

`add` refuses a body whose decisions lack their headings or table of contents
(exit 4, nothing written; for a `decision` it is `/format-decision` rule FD-12). `held_cli.py
validate` refuses an item whose decisions lack them or are stale, an open item whose heading reads
approved, and an aggregate whose decision heading has no `held-` anchor or no table of contents
link; `validate docs/held` checks every item and aggregate in the store.
`scripts/format_decision_check.py` reports FD-12 on a held item file. Each refusal names the fix,
`held_cli.py toc <file>` for an item and `compile` for an aggregate.

## Lifecycle

```text
open  --(the repo owner answers in chat or under ## Answer)-->  answered  --(folded in)-->  retired
```

1. **open**: written and shipped. The owning session replays it in full until it is answered
   (§ Replay); everyone else sees path + ask + the `**Open decision:**` block.
2. **answered**: the repo owner answered. The owning session transcribes a chat answer verbatim under
   `## Answer` with its timestamp (or he wrote there himself), records the answer in its durable
   home (a `bd` comment on the task, a Decision in the design or plan doc), then runs
   `held_cli.py answer <path> --text-file <f> [--recorded-in <ref>]`, which sets `status: answered`,
   `answered_at` and, when the durable home already exists, `answer_recorded_in`.
   An `answered` item the session has not yet acted on is a prod condition for the chief.
3. **retired**: the answer is folded in and acted on. `held_cli.py retire <path> --recorded-in
   <ref>` performs the `git rm`; it refuses an `open` item and refuses without `--recorded-in`, so
   every retired item names where its answer lives: in `answer_recorded_in` when it was set at
   answer time, and always in the retiring commit's message. The directory holds only live items;
   history is `git log --all -- docs/held/<machine>--<slug>/`.

Retirement checks the landing pad is clean, the item's path and frontmatter are valid, its
status is `answered`, and `--recorded-in` is nonempty. It always rechecks any `superseded by
<held-path>` target: the target must exist, have valid held metadata and the same kind, and,
for a decision, pass the current explanation and authority checks. It does not revalidate the
unchanged question. The saved answer's authority claims are rechecked unless the last commit
changing this item contains `answer`'s exact `docs(held): answered <filename>` record and
`Answer recorded <answered_at>.` timestamp (including those retained in a squash commit body).
An unchanged committed answer can therefore retire even if authority checks became stricter
after it was recorded. A hand-edited answer without that matching record must pass today's
checks. New `answer` writes always run authority checks. Retirement writes only the deletion
and the commit recording the durable reference; the normal commit hooks still run.

## Replay

The rule is keyed on **who is displaying**, not on the item and not on the store:

| Displayer | Form |
|---|---|
| the owning session (the one whose `session` the item carries) | the body **in full**, via `held_cli.py show <path>`, in one fenced block under the header `Held output (replayed): <path> — ask: <ask>`; never a summary, never "as noted earlier", never the path alone |
| the chief, `/fleet-brief`, any `SendMessage`, a re-surface of an `answered` item | path + ask (`Held for you:` / `Ask:`, § What the chat says) + the `**Open decision:**` block for a decision; never the body |

The owning session replays every `open` item of its own at **every window start** until it is
`answered` (plan D-5): the SessionStart hook `held-replay-session-start.sh` lists them and
`/auto-start` Step 4 replays them, oldest first, once per window; `show <path>` replays one on
demand. An `answered` item is shown as its path plus "answered <answered_at>; record, act, retire".
A session's items are looked for in **every store this machine routes to**, not only the one its
current checkout routes to (D-10): `list --session <id> --json` with no `--repo` walks every store
and every landing pad for the session, and `show` takes the absolute path `list` printed, whichever
repository it lies in. A `**Open decision:**` block closes every message while a decision is open,
as `/format-decision` requires, and it carries the decision's `Recorded in:` path. The replay cost
is bounded by the session's own duty to transcribe an answer the moment it arrives (below) and by
§ Supersession, which the hook applies at read time: of the briefing kinds (`summary`, `exit-goal`,
`fleet-brief`, `progress-review`) only the newest open item of each kind is listed to replay, and
every older one is listed under `superseded briefings` by path, never replayed ((internal ref): kg-2
held 52 open items, 291 KB, 32 of them briefings, and could not replay them in one window; the repo owner
2026-10-14, "don't show me anything superseded"). The hook prints each item's byte count so the
cost is visible before it is paid.

## Answering, partial answers and supersession

**Answering.** A reply the repo owner gives in chat is transcribed verbatim, with its timestamp, into a
text file and recorded with `answer <path> --text-file <f> [--recorded-in <ref>]` in the same turn.
An acknowledgement ("read it", "ok", "noted") answers a briefing (`progress-review`, `summary`,
`exit-goal`, `fleet-brief`); the `--recorded-in` for a retired briefing with no durable home of its
own is the answer commit (`commit <sha>` from the `answer` verb's JSON).

Answering a legacy decision needs no re-issue in the checked chat form. `ship` compares its
merge-base and tip bytes, exempting changes confined to `status`, `answered_at`,
`answer_recorded_in` and text under the final `## Answer` heading. Its existing findings remain
visible as non-blocking findings. Any other changed byte requires the complete decision package.
Answering and then retiring a legacy decision, including one superseded by a checked replacement,
also ships. `retire` deletes the item and preserves its answer commit in history; it writes no
frontmatter fields.

**Partial answers (D-5).** When a reply answers part of an item, do not edit the original's body.
Write a new item carrying the unanswered remainder (same `kind`, the title suffixed `(remaining)`,
`ask` naming what is still open), then answer the original with the partial text and
`--recorded-in <the new item's path>`. The new item replays; the old one does not, and the
`answer_recorded_in` chain from the original to the remainder is the audit trail.

**Supersession (D-9, widened by (internal ref)).** A fresh briefing (`progress-review`, `summary`,
`exit-goal`, `fleet-brief`) supersedes the same session's earlier unanswered ones of the same kind,
because each re-reports the session's state at the time it is written: a newer one carries forward
every ask of the older ones that is still open (each open decision is its own held item and is
indexed, never folded in). The replay hook already lists the older ones as superseded; record it
when convenient: answer each with the text `superseded by <new path>` and retire it with
`--recorded-in <new path>`, in that order. A decision never supersedes: it is its own question.
Decided by aih-firstmate-1 (Opus 5.5) under `/decision-framework` on the repo owner's 2026-10-14
instruction; the earlier rule that only `progress-review` supersedes let a long-running session's
open set outgrow one window.

**A held decision that a later decision made moot ((internal ref)).** Who caused the supersession
decides what happens to the old item. the repo owner, 2026-10-15: superseded items caused by "my feedback and
human made decisions" need no review, while "ai /decision-framework decisions that would lead to
superseded decision should be reviewed". Three cases, each pinned by
`tests/test_held_supersession_cases.py`. They apply to `decision` items only. The briefing kinds
(`fleet-brief`, `progress-review`, `summary`, `exit-goal`) keep the superseded-by-newer-briefing
rule above and never go through case 2.

1. **the repo owner caused it.** His own later decision, answer or feedback settled the old item's question,
   even when an agent then worked out the details. Answer the old item with the text
   `superseded by the repo owner's <date> decision: <what replaced it> (<ref>)` and retire it with
   `--recorded-in <ref>`, in that order. It is never re-surfaced for review.
2. **An agent's ruling caused it.** An agent's `/decision-framework` ruling made the old item moot
   on its own. A ruling his feedback asked for is case 1, not this one. The old item stays in front
   of him for review. Add one `decision` item titled `AI-superseded: <old title>`, with `ask` "Retire
   it, or keep it open". Its body carries the old item's decision verbatim and the new ruling in
   `/format-decision` form. Add an `/explain` that covers four things: what the old decision was, why
   it was made then, why the new ruling supersedes it, and how the new ruling still meets the old
   need. Leave the old item open. When the repo owner answers, record his answer on the review item and
   retire it. If he says retire, answer and retire the old item with `--recorded-in <review path>`.
   If he says keep, the old item stays open and replays as an ordinary decision.
3. **the repo owner overrides an earlier decision.** His new decision reverses an earlier one, whether an
   agent's or his own. Show the override in the same response that records his decision, not later.
   Quote the old decision and `/explain` the same four points. Record the override in the governing
   doc's decision entry and Approval Log, and name the old decision there. If the old decision is an
   open held item, it then follows case 1.

The replay hook lists items by path, never by title. So add the case 2 item without `--topic`: the
title then becomes the file's slug (`...-decision-ai-superseded-<old title>.md`), and the item
reaches the repo owner through the normal replay with no extra mechanism. A case 2 item that the repo owner answers
is case 1 from then on.

**Finding the held items a ruling moots ((internal ref)).** A ruling is often recorded by a different
session from the one holding the item it moots, in a design's Approval Log, a Beads comment or a
Teams draft's status, and nothing linked the two: three held decisions were shown to the repo owner again
on 2026-10-16 after he had ruled on each. Two checks close that gap.

- **Sweep when you record a ruling.** In the same turn that you record one of the repo owner's rulings, or
   a supersession, run `held_cli.py list --status open --mentions <decision id> --mentions
   <governing doc path> --json` with no `--repo`, so every routed store is read. Apply case 1, 2 or
   3 to each hit. Update notes for every Beads issue named by the escalation and reconcile its
   CC panel title in the same turn, clearing stale decision blockers and naming the ruling
   record. The answer command prints all linked tasks for this sweep. A hit held by another live session goes to that session as a message naming the
   item's path and the ruling's record. Settle it yourself only when that session has exited.
- **Compile checks each open decision's record.** `compile` reads every `Recorded in:` target
   `<path>#<anchor>` this host can open. A target whose decision heading or first `> **Decision:**`
   line now reads Superseded, `✅ Approved` or CLOSED is reported on stderr and under `settled` in
   the JSON. The item stays in the compiled doc, because only the session can tell case 1 from
   case 2. Settle each reported item before the doc or the item is shown again. An item with an
   open `AI-superseded:` review item is case 2 already and is not reported.

## Decisions are git-tracked before they are shown

Every blocker needing owner input and every escalated decision reaches the repo owner only as a git-tracked held `decision` with `/format-decision` + a full `/explain`, shipped to main and listed in the session's compiled held doc before its absolute path is reported.

Use `## Explanation` with substantive `### Orientation`, `### Mechanism`, `### Rationale`, `### Boundaries` and `### Consequences` sections. Cite sources for project claims. Run `scripts/held_decision_check.py check <item>` as well as the strict format checker. Structural checks do not prove explanation quality or semantic fidelity.

`send` refuses incomplete explanations. `answer --escalated-to-sergei` validates the original
item, keeps it open for the repo owner, compiles and ships before printing its absolute path. A failed
ship is not a completed handoff. Run compile and ship after repairing it; do not send the path first.

The always-running `held-decision-integrity` pre-commit hook reads the index, including deleted
paths. `held_cli ship` repeats the check before publishing. An open decision cannot disappear
without a surviving answer record or an `AI-superseded:` review linked by `Old held: <old path>`.
Case 2 still requires keeping the original open beside its review. The deletion guard is a
minimum audit-trail check, not authority to retire an unanswered item.

Gate 0 claims and restrictions attributed to the repo owner name the canonical founding ask and carry
`Gate 0 quote: <verbatim human requirement>`. The quote must occur in a human FAR entry. Read
the ask too: a matching quote does not establish that the claimed restriction follows from it.

the repo owner, 2026-10-12 (`(internal ref)`): "they should all be documented in their appropriate /doc
--kind design or plan or analysis or bug or audit or whatever kind of doc is appropriate or at
least a held doc file ... decisions should be documented somewhere and git tracked ... surface all
the decisions to me (after writing them all to a held doc file that has all of them compiled
together so you can resurface them to me ...)."

A decision reaches the repo owner only after it has a record in a git commit, in this order, per decision:

1. **Record.** When a design, plan, analysis, bug or audit doc governs the subject (the doc exists,
   or `/doc --kind` says one should: a sub-system or feature with a doc has its decisions there),
   write the Decision block into that doc (`docs/designs/TEMPLATE.md` § Design Decisions: the
   Decision Summary row, the per-option layout, the fixed-key `decision-record` comment, the
   `PENDING` marker) and commit it in the session's worktree. When no doc governs (an operational
   call, a one-off, a question about a tool or a run), the held item written in step 2 is the
   record, and nothing else needs to be created for it.
2. **Hold.** `held_cli.py add --kind decision ...` with the body the message will show (§ Holding
   at emit time). The `add` commit is the git-tracked record for a decision with no governing
   doc; a decision with one now has two tracked copies, and the doc is canonical.
3. **Compile.** Regenerate this session's aggregate held review doc in the store the item landed
   in (§ The aggregate compiled held doc below) and commit it in the landing pad.
4. **Ship.** `ship --session <id>`: a `decision` item ships at once (plan (internal ref) D-2), and the
   aggregate rides the same ship.
5. **Emit.** The message ends with three lines, each a link (§ Links) whose display text is the
   absolute path of a file that is already in a commit:

   ```text
   Recorded in: [<governing doc path>#<anchor>](<relative path>#<anchor>)      (or: [<held item path>](<its file name>) (this held item is the decision's record; no other document governs it))
   Held: [<held item path>](<its file name>)
   Compiled in: [<aggregate held review doc path, docs/held/<host>--<slug>-held-review.md>](../<its file name>)
   ```

`not yet documented`, `TBD`, "will be recorded after you decide" and a path that does not exist
yet are each a defect: write the record, then send the message. The `**Open decision:**` block
`/format-decision` requires carries the `Recorded in:` path. The rule covers every decision
presented to the repo owner as open or for his review, through `/format-decision`, `/exit-goal`,
`/progress-review` or `/summary`. A decision an AI resolved under the Authority test is not one of
them: it is recorded where it was resolved (`decision-framework.md` § Recording a self-resolved
item; `resolve` when no doc governs) and is not held, compiled, indexed or listed for the repo owner
(`decision-framework.md` § An AI-resolved decision is not put in front of the repo owner). `add` refuses a
`decision` item whose title or own first decision line records `✅ Resolved by`, naming `resolve`;
an `AI-superseded:` item (case 2 above) is the one exception, because he asked for those. `compile`
leaves an older such item out of the compiled doc and names it on stderr and under `ai_resolved`
in its JSON; answer it `AI-resolved; not for review` and retire it with `--recorded-in` its record. A sub-agent never records or holds for the repo owner itself: it reports the
decision to its launcher, which runs the five steps (§ Who writes here). Steps 2 and 5 are
checked: the held body is the byte copy of the emitted block (the shape is
`docs/prompts/held/decision/TEMPLATE.md`), so its three lines sit before the block's end marker,
with `Held:` and `Compiled in:` as `add --plan` prints them; `add --kind decision` refuses a body
that fails `scripts/format_decision_check.py --form chat` or names other paths, and step 5 runs
`format_decision_check.py --form chat --strict` on the full message before it is sent.

### The aggregate compiled held doc

One file per session per store, at a fixed name beside the session's item directory:
`docs/held/<machine>--<slug>-held-review.md` (design
[📄 ai-harness/docs/designs/held-doc-review-and-canonical-readme-sync.md](../designs/held-doc-review-and-canonical-readme-sync.md)
D-2, which replaced the decisions-only `-open-decisions.md` of plan (internal ref) D-12 and kept its
one-file-per-session-per-store rule). It gathers every item of the session in that store that is
`open` or `answered` and not yet retired, of every kind, so the repo owner can be shown all of it again in
one place. It is a compiled copy: each decision's canonical record is the path its `Recorded in:`
line names, and every body in it is a byte copy except one mechanical change: each relative
link target is re-pointed from the item's directory to the aggregate's, one level up, so it opens
the same file, and `compile` warns, naming the item and link, when that file does not exist
((internal ref)). A session that holds into two stores (plan
(internal ref) D-10) has one aggregate in each, and each names the other's path in its `other_store`
frontmatter key. Regenerate it after every `add`, `answer` or `retire`, and at `/save-state` Step
0.7.

`held_cli.py compile --session <id>` does that in every routed store. It reads the session's items
from `list --session <id>` (the landing pad's view), renders
[📄 ai-harness/docs/prompts/held/review/TEMPLATE.md.jinja](../prompts/held/review/TEMPLATE.md.jinja)
with jinja2 and `StrictUndefined`, writes or `git rm`s the doc in the pad, commits it, and reports
`written`, `removed` or `unchanged` per store with the open and answered counts. It removes the doc
when the session has no open or answered item left in that store. In the commit that writes or
removes it, it also `git rm`s the session's own legacy `<machine>--<slug>-open-decisions.md`, and
never another session's. The Regenerated stamp and the Update Log are kept while the rest of the
file is byte-equal, so a re-run with nothing changed commits nothing. Held item and other-store
paths are the stable main-tree paths, valid once `ship` lands the pad. Every path it prints outside
an inlined body (each `Held:` and `Recorded in:` line, the Index's `Canonical record` and `Held
item` cells, Other held items, Escalated to a decider, Answered items and Superseded briefings) is a
link, `[<absolute main-tree path>](<path relative to docs/held/>)`, an anchor kept on both halves
(§ Links); a bare `Recorded in:` from an item held before the link rule is rendered the same way.

What it selects, section by section, in this order:

| Section | What it holds |
|---|---|
| frontmatter | `title`, `category: held-doc-review`, `tags`, `status` (`open` or `answered`), `source` (`held_cli.py compile, <stamp>`), `template_version: "held-doc-review-1.0.0"`, `session`, `store`, `other_store`, `counts` |
| `## Table of Contents` | every `##` and `###` of the doc, each blocker's included, and every decision's `####`, each linking its `held-` anchor (§ Decision headings and the approved marker) |
| `## Executive Summary` | generated: the oldest open ask first, then the counts, answered items included |
| `## Latest summary`, `## Latest exit-goal`, `## Current progress review`, `## Fleet brief` | the newest open item of each briefing kind, its `Held:` line and its body in full; `None open.` otherwise; `## Fleet brief` only when the session holds one |
| `## Open blockers` | every open `blocker`, a `###` with its title, its `Held:` line and its body in full |
| `## Open decisions` | `### Index` (`Id`, `Decision`, `Recommendation`, `Canonical record`, `Held item`: the id is the task, else a `D-N` in the title, else the file stem; pipes escaped; with no `Recorded in:` line the record is the held item, `(this held item is the decision's record; no other document governs it)`; a `Recorded in:` that is the item's own landing-pad `Held:` path is shown at its main-tree path like the `Held item` column, so it survives the pad's reap), then `### Decisions, in full`: per decision its anchor `<a id="held-<item file stem slug>"></a>`, `#### <Id>: <title>` (with the approved marker when its record reads `✅ Approved`), its `Recorded in:` line, its body as `show` prints it, `---` |
| `## Other held items` | every open `other` item: title, ask, path; bodies are linked, never inlined; then, only when one is open, `### Escalated to a decider`: the table of decisions addressed to another decider, and per decision its anchor and `#### <Id>: <title>` |
| `## Answered, not yet retired` | `### Answered items`: every answered item of every kind with its `answered_at`, its durable record or `not recorded`, its path and the action left before `retire`; then `### Answered decisions`: per answered `decision` its anchor, `#### <Id>: <title> ✅ Approved <date>` and one line naming its path, `answered_at` and durable record |
| `## Superseded briefings` | every older open briefing by path, with the newer one that supersedes it; never replayed (§ Replay) |
| `## References` | one `[📄 <repo>/<relpath>](<relative path>)` backlink per compiled item, then this README, `docs/procedures/held-doc-review.md` and `skills/held-doc-review/SKILL.md` |
| `## Update Log` | one row per regeneration that changed the doc (`Regenerated (UTC)`, `Items`, `Change`), newest first, the last 20 kept; `git log` is the full history |

Every inlined body sits between `<!-- held-review:item path="<relpath>" -->` and
`<!-- /held-review:item -->`; headings inside a body are the item's own and are not in the table
of contents. The regions are `overview`, `briefings`, `blockers` and `decisions` (replaceable) and
`update_log` (append only). The human-readable shape is
[📄 ai-harness/docs/prompts/held/review/TEMPLATE.md](../prompts/held/review/TEMPLATE.md), and
`/doc --kind held-doc-review` scaffolds the same shape by hand where compile cannot run.

The Executive Summary and the decisions Index are what `/auto-start` Step 4 prints after the full
replay of each open item; the SessionStart hook names the file by path and byte count. Both names
are reserved in the core (`held_output.RESERVED_SUFFIXES` = `-held-review.md`, `-open-decisions.md`),
so an unfiltered `list` neither parses either as an item nor reports it `malformed`. The
reservation covers only files directly in `docs/held/`: an item in its session's directory whose
title ends in "held review" or "open decisions" keeps that name and is listed, compiled,
validated and link-checked like any other item (`held_output.is_reserved`).

## Templates per kind

Each `kind` has a canonical body shape and a brief, named in
[📄 ai-harness/config/held_kinds.toml](../../config/held_kinds.toml) and indexed in
[📄 ai-harness/docs/prompts/held/README.md](../prompts/held/README.md):

| Kind | TEMPLATE (the body shape) | STUB (the brief that produces one) |
|---|---|---|
| `decision` | `docs/prompts/held/decision/TEMPLATE.md` | `docs/prompts/held/decision/STUB.md` |
| `blocker` | `docs/prompts/held/blocker/TEMPLATE.md` | `docs/prompts/held/blocker/STUB.md` |
| `exit-goal` | `docs/prompts/held/exit-goal/TEMPLATE.md` | `docs/prompts/held/exit-goal/STUB.md` |
| `progress-review` | `docs/prompts/held/progress-review/TEMPLATE.md` | `docs/prompts/held/progress-review/STUB.md` |
| `summary` | `docs/prompts/summary-report/TEMPLATE.md` | `docs/prompts/held/summary/STUB.md` |
| `fleet-brief` | `docs/prompts/held/fleet-brief/TEMPLATE.md` | `docs/prompts/held/fleet-brief/STUB.md` |
| `other` | `docs/prompts/held/other/TEMPLATE.md` (explain and report) | `docs/prompts/held/other/STUB.md` |

A producing skill's output is the held body, so the skill's output format and its kind's TEMPLATE
are one text, and the TEMPLATE is canonical. Each TEMPLATE opens with
`<!-- template_version: held-<kind>-1.0.0 -->`, states the kind's default `ask`, and carries its
body between `<!-- held:<kind>:begin -->` and `<!-- held:<kind>:end -->`. A body that holds a
decision carries its generated heading and table of contents (§ Decision headings and the
approved marker). Each TEMPLATE and STUB carries the two § Links sentences in an HTML comment, and every path or URL placeholder in a body
shape is already a link. `add` runs a kind row's
`validator` on the staged body before it writes anything (`decision` names
`scripts/format_decision_check.py`); `compile` reads the rows marked `supersedes = true` as the
briefing kinds. `held_output.load_kind_registry()` refuses the table when its kinds and
`held_output.KINDS` differ.

## `/held-doc-review`

`/held-doc-review` brings everything a session holds for one goal up to date and compiles it into
the session's aggregate held review doc: the current `/progress-review`, the `/summary` of the
goal's batch across compaction windows with every task completed since the last `/exit-goal`
folded in, and every blocker or decision needing owner review as a checked `decision` item. The
unvalidated `blocker` kind is reserved for operational status requiring no owner input. Then it
runs `compile` and `ship` and prints the aggregate's
Executive Summary and decisions Index. Its modes are `review` (on request), `save-state`
(`/save-state` Step 0.7, before every compaction, where a briefing is regenerated only when its
change check fires) and `exit` (`/exit-goal`). Skill:
[📄 ai-harness/skills/held-doc-review/SKILL.md](../../skills/held-doc-review/SKILL.md). Procedure,
with the two change checks and § Propagation review:
[📄 ai-harness/docs/procedures/held-doc-review.md](../procedures/held-doc-review.md).

The path-scoped rule `held-docs.md` (source
`projects-wide-session-config/rules/held-docs.md`) loads whenever a session touches
`docs/held/`, and sends it to this README first. It reaches a session two ways, with the same
bytes: ai-harness installs it into `~/.claude/rules/`, and the canonical-README sync copies it into
project-template's `.claude/rules/`, from where copier propagation carries it to every consumer
repository, so a host without ai-harness still loads it. That copy is held with this README's
fallback copy until D-8 of the design is answered, and both reach project-template in one PR.

## Writing, shipping, listing

All verbs are `~/projects/ai-harness/.venv/bin/python ~/projects/ai-harness/scripts/held_cli.py <verb>`,
by those absolute paths from whatever directory you stand in, never a relative
`scripts/held_cli.py`: `add` derives its source repo from that directory, and a relative form only
runs inside an ai-harness checkout, which routed every kg-*session's items to ai-harness
((internal ref)). When the derived repo is not the one the session slug's `task_prefix` names in
`config/fleet-projects.toml` (`kg-1` is `bms-semantic-knowledge-graph`) and the two route to
different stores, `add` refuses (exit 4, nothing written) naming both; pass `--source-repo` to hold
there on purpose ((internal ref): a warning still let a kg-* exit item land in an ai-harness pad). Exact flags: `held_cli.py <verb> --help`. Every verb
takes `--json`. `--repo <checkout>` exists on `add` (the checkout whose registered repo name is
the default `--source-repo`) and on `list` (read ONE checkout's `docs/held/` instead of every
routed store); `answer`, `retire` and `ship` take no `--repo`, because the item path or the
routing table already names the store (T-12 dropped it under the pre-v1 no-compat rule).
`stores --json` names every destination this machine's table routes to, each with its repo,
destination, absolute store path, `land` mode and whether the directory is present. A file named
`*-held-review.md` (the aggregate) or `*-open-decisions.md` (the legacy digest it replaced)
directly in `docs/held/` is reserved and is neither an item nor malformed, exactly like
`README.md`; the same name inside a session directory is an item; `RESERVED_SUFFIXES` beside `README_NAME` in `held_output.py` carries both suffixes. `add`, `answer` and `retire` take
`--provenance-file <f>`, the commit's trailer block, defaulting to `Delegated-to: none`; it is
validated before anything is written. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 a step failed (its stderr printed
verbatim), 2 a bad input, 3 `held_root_missing`, 4 refused. Tests override the table, the registry
and the projects root through the routing module's own `ASK_FIDELITY_ARTIFACT_ROUTING`,
`ASK_FIDELITY_PROJECT_REGISTRY` and `ASK_FIDELITY_PROJECTS_DIR`.

When the forge refuses a merge because the base branch was modified, `ship` re-reads the PR by retrying `gh pr merge` up to three total attempts; every other merge refusal stops immediately, and the final forge error is preserved verbatim.

| Step | Command | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| write | `add --kind <k> --session <s>@<m> --task <id> --title "<t>" --ask "<a>" --source-skill "<skill + args>" --body-file <f> [--topic <slug>] [--unchecked] [--plan]` | `--plan` (no `--body-file`) writes nothing and prints `Held: [<item path>](<its file name>)` and `Compiled in: [<compiled held doc path>](../<its file name>)`, the two lines a decision body carries in link form (§ Links), from the same allocation `add` runs, and its JSON carries them as `held_line` and `compiled_line` beside the bare `path` and `compiled`; for every kind, `add` refuses a body with a bare path or URL (exit 4, the `HL-01`/`HL-02` lines on stderr, nothing written; § Links), and `--unchecked` holds it printing the same lines; for `--kind decision`, `add` first runs the `/format-decision` check (`scripts/format_decision_check.py --form chat`) on the body and refuses a failing one, or one whose `Held:`/`Compiled in:` are not those paths (exit 4, the checker's `<path>:<line>: FD-NN ... Fix: ...` lines on stderr, nothing written); `--unchecked` is for the capture-repair route only and holds the body anyway, printing the same lines; refuses a landing pad with any uncommitted change (as `answer` and `retire` do), then writes the file into the session's landing-pad worktree (below) and commits the whole index with the provenance trailer block, so what the pre-commit hooks stage (the display-id owner ledger) rides in the item commit and the pad is left clean; prints the absolute path |
| stores | `stores --json` | every destination this machine's `[[held_routes]]` table routes to: repo, destination, absolute store path, `land`, present or absent |
| link | `link --session <s>@<m> [--source-repo <repo>] [--absolute] <absolute path>[#anchor]...` | prints the Markdown link a held body of that session writes for each file, relative to the session's item directory in its routed store's main tree: `[📄 <repo>/<relpath>](<relative>)` in the store's repository, plus ` ([GitHub](<url>))` for another repository with a GitHub origin, `[📄 <absolute path>](<relative>)` outside every repository; `--absolute` shows the absolute path as display text; run outside any git checkout without `--source-repo`, it routes by the repo the session's prefix names; a path that is not absolute or `~` exits 2 (§ Links) |
| ship | `ship --session <s>@<m>` | for every store holding this session's landing pad, by that store's `land` mode, after first dropping the pad's oldest commits whose content is already on the target (the squash-merge content proof `worktree_audit.unlanded_added_lines`: a landing routed around `ship` leaves them under other shas, and pushed beside new commits they make the squash fail "the merge commit cannot be cleanly created") by anchoring the old HEAD under a local `refs/backup/<date>/held-pad-rebuild/<branch>/<sha>` and rebasing only the rest onto the target; a pad with nothing left resets onto the target and reports `nothing-to-ship`, and a conflict restores the pad and refuses as `pad-behind-target` ((internal ref)), except that a rebase stop (here or in the catch-up below) confined to `.beads/display-id-owners.tsv` is resolved as the sorted, de-duplicated union of both sides' rows and continued, because each held commit appends ledger rows the moved target may already carry ((internal ref)): `pr` pushes `wt/<m>--<s>/held-<s>`, opens or updates the PR (`ghp`, the personal identity), and when the diff against `origin/main` touches only `docs/held/**`, the resolution log (`docs/decisions/resolutions/**`) and the `.beads/` bookkeeping the pre-commit ledger hook stages squash-merges it; before that push it rebases the pad onto the fetched target when the target moved, the same catch-up `push` runs, because a stale base carries `.beads/` mirrors missing the target's newer rows and the pre-push append-only gate refuses it ((internal ref)), and it drops the pad's tracking ref for its own branch once the forge has deleted the branch after the previous squash merge, which the pre-push guard otherwise refuses ((internal ref)), and when the pad no longer fast-forwards the pad branch's published tip and that tip is one this run rewrote (an ancestor of the pre-ship HEAD) or is already on the target by content, it pushes to and opens the PR from the first `<branch>-r<N>` absent on origin instead, leaving the tip and any PR on it alone until that PR lands, and names the route in the payload's `push_route` (`pad-branch` or `fresh-branch`, (internal ref)); after the reset it re-checks that test against the fetched target and, when the remote pad branch still reads that tip, anchors it under `refs/backup/<date>/held-pad/<branch>`, reads it back, deletes the branch leased on the tip and drops its tracking ref, so the next ship uses the pad branch and the shipped pad's reap does not refuse that copy `KEEP_BACKUP_COPY_DIVERGED` (`retire_routed_tip`, (internal ref)), and when the merge left the remote branch behind at a MERGED PR's head (and not an ancestor of the pad), anchors that tip under `refs/backup/<date>/held-pad/<branch>` and deletes the branch, leased on the tip; a tip that is no merged PR's head is left alone and the push refuses ((internal ref)), and after the catch-up rebase and before its push it retires a stranded backup copy by the same test, anchor and leased delete `push` runs after its reset (below), because in a PR store that copy is the branch the push updates and the rebase leaves it a non-fast-forward; a copy holding any commit the pad's pre-catch-up HEAD lacks is left alone and the push refuses ((internal ref)); in either mode, when the pre-push sync-deletion guard would read the push as losing paths that the target retired and that lie outside this session's own `docs/held/<m>--<s>/` (and its aggregate and legacy digest), whether other sessions' held items ((internal ref)) or tracked files outside `docs/held/` the pad never writes ((internal ref)), each absent at the target tip, it first adds an empty pad commit declaring each with a `Sync-deletion-accepted: <path>` line; an own path, or one the target still has, is never declared and the push refuses with the guard's full text in the step's `stderr`; `push` fast-forwards the pad branch onto the target branch only when the diff is that same scope and makes no forge call, first rebasing the pad onto the fetched target when another session's ship moved it (sessions write disjoint directories, so this replays cleanly; a conflict aborts the rebase, leaves the pad as it was and refuses as `pad-behind-target`, (internal ref)); both prove each `docs/held/` and resolution-log path by content (`git cat-file -e origin/main:<path>` and the blob; absence for a retire) and each `.beads/` path present (a squash onto a moved ledger lands a merged blob) and resets the landing pad onto `origin/main`. After that reset `push` retires the pad's remote backup copy (`origin:refs/heads/<pad branch>`, which the backup reconciler pushed while the pad was ahead and then skips once it is integrated) when the catch-up rebase stranded it: a copy that is not an ancestor of the reset pad but is an ancestor of the pad's pre-ship HEAD is anchored under `refs/backup/<date>/held-pad/<branch>`, read back and deleted leased on its tip, so the shipped pad reaps without a hand step; a copy holding any commit the shipped pad did not is left alone and the reap still refuses it `KEEP_BACKUP_COPY_DIVERGED` ((internal ref)). Last, `push` fast-forwards the store's main tree, the copy the repo owner reads, to the target with `merge --ff-only` when that tree is clean and on the target branch, and otherwise leaves it exactly as it was and names why in the `main_tree` step, which never fails the ship ((internal ref)). Any other diff stops at the open PR and says so. Each `git fetch origin` a ship or add runs is run again, up to three tries, while it loses a local ref-lock race to another fetch on the host (`cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/...'`), so a merged item is never reported failed for it; any other fetch failure, or a race still lost on the last try, fails the step ((internal ref)). Every step's verbatim failure is printed and stops the rest. With `AIH_HELD_GH_CMD` unset and `ghp` unusable (not on PATH, or `~/.config/gh-personal` missing), `sergeiwallace/*` destinations use plain `gh` after verifying its login is `sergeiwallace` before any push |
| manual ship | `/sync-git worktree:<landing-pad path>` | the push step by hand; the PR and merge then follow the ordinary integration rules |
| compile | `compile --session <s>@<m>` | regenerates the session's aggregate held review doc (§ The aggregate compiled held doc) in every routed store, from the session's items of every kind that are `open` or `answered`: writes it in the landing pad and commits, or `git rm`s and commits when none is left, removing the session's own legacy `-open-decisions.md` in the same commit; no push (that is `ship`); prints the path, `written` \| `removed` \| `unchanged` and the open and answered counts per store; leaves out an AI-resolved decision and names it under `ai_resolved`, and names under `settled` each open decision whose `Recorded in:` target now reads Superseded, `✅ Approved` or CLOSED (§ Answering, partial answers and supersession); exit 3 only when every store's `docs/held/` is missing |
| list | `list [--status open\|answered\|all] [--session <id>] [--task <id>] [--repo <checkout>] [--mentions <decision id or doc path>]... --json` | `--mentions` keeps only items whose file names one of the values as a whole token (`D-24` never matches `D-240`), the sweep for a newly recorded ruling; every item under every routed store's `docs/held/` (or one checkout's with `--repo`); with `--session`, a store where that session's landing pad exists is read from the pad, so an added but unshipped item and pad-only answered or retired state are current, and an item byte-identical to the main tree's copy is printed at its main-tree path ((internal ref)); each tagged with its `store`, with its path and frontmatter; unparseable files under `malformed` with the error; a missing `docs/held/` is `held_root_missing`, never an empty list |
| answer | `answer <path> --text-file <f> [--recorded-in <ref>]` | appends under `## Answer`, sets `answered` + `answered_at` (and `answer_recorded_in` when given), marks each decision's heading approved except those an open remainder item named by `--recorded-in` carries forward, commits; refuses an item that is not `open` |
| retire | `retire <path> --recorded-in <ref>` | `git rm` + commit; checks clean pad, path/frontmatter, answered status, nonempty ref and current superseding records; rechecks answer authority unless the last item-changing commit retains the matching answer-command record (§ Lifecycle) |
| resolve | `resolve --session <s>@<m> --decision-id <id> --question "<q>" --option "a: <label>" --option "b: <label>" --chosen <letter> --rationale "<r>" --criterion "<c>" --confidence high\|medium\|low --ai-family <f> --ai-model <m> --ai-effort <e> --ai-profile <p> [--task <id>] [--source-repo <repo>]` | appends one self-resolved ad-hoc decision to `docs/decisions/resolutions/<host-alias>/<slug>/resolutions-<slug>@<host-alias>-<date>.jsonl` in the routed store's landing pad and commits it ((internal ref) D-4 (a)); routed like `add`, so a (employer ref) session's row stays in its (employer ref) store (D-3 (a)); `ship` lands it with the session's held items; refuses a host with no alias in `config/machine-host-aliases.toml`, a `--chosen` that is not an `--option` letter, and a blank rationale or criterion |
| migrate | `migrate --old <slug> --new <slug> [--machine <m>] [--dry-run] [--provenance-file <f>]` | carries a renamed session's held state to its new name in every routed store ((internal ref) T-04); see the paragraph below the table |
| migrate-machine | `migrate-machine --old <machine> --new <machine> [--since <ISO-8601 UTC instant>] [--dry-run] [--provenance-file <f>]` | renames every session of one machine across routed stores, with one commit per session pad, one reviewed run per store; see below |
| restamp | `restamp [--dry-run] [--json]` | in every routed store, repairs each landing-pad branch's `branch.<pad branch>.aih-agent-worktree` stamp that names a path that no longer exists: re-stamps it to the worktree that has the branch checked out, unsets it when the branch is gone, and leaves it (reported `keep`) when the branch is checked out nowhere; a stamp whose path exists is never touched ((internal ref)). It also rewrites each checked-out pad's `aih-provenance.json` `owner_session` (reported `reown <branch> <old> -> <new>`) when it names a session other than the one the pad's branch names, and reports a missing or unreadable record as `keep <branch> provenance missing\|unreadable, left alone` without writing it ((internal ref)) |
| toc | `toc <file> [--kind <k>] [--title "<the add --title>"]` | writes each decision's generated heading and the generated table of contents into a staged body or a held item, in place, and prints `written` or `unchanged`; keeps every heading it already wrote; on a held item it sets the approved marker from the item's own status (§ Decision headings and the approved marker) |
| validate | `validate <path or directory>...` | schema check, naming the first violated key, plus § Decision headings and the approved marker for every item and aggregate; a directory is every item and aggregate under it (`README.md` and a legacy digest skipped); prints `<n> valid, <m> invalid` for more than one file and exits 1 on any invalid one |
| show | `show <path> [--json]` | prints the item's body again in full, byte for byte (everything below the frontmatter, `## Answer` included); `--json` returns `{path, frontmatter, body}`. Reads only; a path outside a `docs/held/` tree or a malformed item exits 2 with the parse error verbatim |
| overview | `/fleet-brief` (the chief's skill) | renders open and answered items beside every session's state |

**`migrate`** is what `ai session-migrate OLD NEW` runs through its drop-in hook
`<ai-cli-utils config>/session-migrate.d/held.toml`, which the private orchestrator's `held-hook`
step (`ai-harness apply --only held-hook`; formerly `install.sh` Step 5q, (internal ref)) writes on
every machine: `--dry-run` while the migration plans (a non-zero exit refuses the whole migration), then
for real once the core moves are done. `--old` and `--new` are bare slugs (`aih-2`, never
`aih-2@<host>` or `<host>--aih-2`; exit 2 otherwise), and `--machine` defaults to this machine's
identity. In each store it moves the old landing pad to the new pad path with `git worktree move`
and renames its branch to `wt/<m>--<new>/held-<new>` after anchoring the tip under
`refs/preserved/session-migrate/<old branch>` (the reference-transaction guard refuses a packed
branch's rename without that anchor), so unshipped commits ride along, and re-stamps the renamed
branch's `aih-agent-worktree` to the new pad path (`git branch -m` carries the old path across,
(internal ref)); with no old pad it creates the new one. Every verb that finds its session's pad
already present re-stamps it the same way when the stamp names a gone path. In the new pad it `git mv`s `docs/held/<m>--<old>/` to `docs/held/<m>--<new>/`,
rewrites each item's `session:` line and nothing else, `git rm`s the old session's aggregate and
legacy digest, writes the new aggregate (its Update Log carried over under a `migrated from`
row), validates every moved item and commits once. Every store is planned before any is
written. An old pad left dirty by its session's exit is not a refusal: a `pad-commit-pending <pad>`
action commits its uncommitted state unchanged, as its own commit, before the pad moves, and a
refused commit restores the pad's index exactly and exits 1 ((internal ref)). It refuses (exit 4,
nothing written in any store) when an old pad has unmerged paths or a merge, rebase, cherry-pick
or revert in progress, a reused new pad is dirty, the new directory
already exists while items remain under the old name, or a rekeyed item fails validation, and
exits 1 the same way when a routed store
is present but unusable; a store with no checkout on this machine holds none of its sessions'
items, so it is reported `absent` and skipped. `--dry-run` prints the same `<store> <action>
<path>` lines and refusals with nothing written.
A moved checkout's venv still names the old path, so its own packages stop importing and the
pad's pre-push test gate fails ((internal ref)). So for the moved pad, and for the session's home
worktree `<store>/.worktrees/<new>` that `ai session-migrate` moved before the hook ran, a
`venv-reinstall <path>` action rewrites a venv-store slot's `.aih-checkout` to the new path and
runs `uv sync --all-extras --reinstall [--locked]` in place; a real `.venv` directory is
reinstalled the same way with no record written. A slot still named for the old leaf is not
renamed in place, because every console-script shebang in it names the slot path; instead
`venv_relocate.ensure` builds `<repo>--<new leaf>`, probes it, swaps `.venv` to it and reclaims
the old-name slot through `worktree_venv.reclaim_venv_slot`, which keeps (and names on stderr) a
slot a live process still runs from ((internal ref)). The same command,
`scripts/venv_relocate.py <checkout> --ensure --apply`, repairs a checkout migrated before this.
A `.venv` linking outside the store refuses (exit 4), and a failed reinstall or re-slot exits 1
naming the checkout and the exact command to run.

**`migrate-machine`** changes the machine part of every matching session address, directory,
aggregate, landing-pad path and branch (for example `framework-fedora` to `fw-lnx`, or `mac`
to `sw-mac`). It discovers old-machine sessions from the store's directories, aggregates and
checked-out pad branches, plans every pad in every routed store before writing, and leaves other
machines' pads and directories alone. It reuses `migrate`'s directory move, item validation,
aggregate compiler and Update Log carry-over, anchors each old branch tip under
`refs/preserved/machine-rename/<old branch>`, moves the worktree, renames its branch and
re-stamps `aih-agent-worktree`. Main-only items get an old-name pad through the existing pad
creation path before it moves; nothing is committed to main. The item frontmatter changes only
`session:` and `machine:`; item bodies remain byte for byte unchanged. Only regenerated aggregates
rewrite moved path components. The decision hook treats a Git-paired rename as the same item only
when those two keys make the exact directory-derived machine substitution and all other bytes
match. Both planning modes run the held hook entries and scripts from the running ai-harness
checkout against each planned commit in a temporary index, with the source checkout as cwd.
Every pad's line names that source, the hook checkout, both hook results and its unshipped-commit
check; all refusals are collected before the plan fails. Normal commit hooks still run.
Ship each session first: planning and apply refuse any pad commit absent from the fetched
`origin/<store branch>`, naming the pad, count and `held_cli.py ship --session <slug>@<old>`.
After moving the pad and renaming its branch, apply fetches that target again and advances a
behind-only pad with `git merge --ff-only` before writing items or committing. The old-tip anchor
remains intact; migration never stashes, resets or rebases the pad.
Use the reverse `--old <new> --new <old>` run to restore item bytes and branch names (commits
and aggregate Update Log rows remain).

Unlike `migrate`, this verb refuses **any dirty pad**, rather than committing its pending work.
It also refuses unmerged paths, merge/rebase/cherry-pick/revert markers (even on a clean pad),
occupied target directories or branches, invalid rekeyed items, conflicting anchors and venv
links outside the venv store. These preflight refusals exit 4 without moving pads or writing items
or journals (fetch can update remote-tracking refs);
present but unusable routed stores also refuse with exit 4. An absent checkout is reported with
its reason and skipped; the last line lists it as `not migrated`. `--since` must be an ISO-8601
UTC instant: an item created later in any affected main or pad directory refuses the whole run.
`--dry-run` moves no pads and writes no items or journals, prints the same `<store> <action> <path>` plan as the real run,
and lists each pad as `done` or `pending`, plus every preflight refusal.

Crash recovery uses a durable write-ahead journal at
`<store>/.git/held-machine-rename/<old>--<new>.json`, outside the pads. At the gap between pads,
the verb writes that pad's preimages and intended bytes **before** moving it. A pad is counted
done only when its new directory, branch and migration commit exist with the intended bytes;
a rerun skips it and resumes pending pads, accepting only journal-owned partial changes.
An interrupted Git step or commit exits 1 and retains the journal for that rerun. As with
`migrate`, a moved pad's venv is refreshed and an unsuccessful refresh reports its repair command;
session home worktrees are unchanged by a machine rename and are not refreshed.
It does not ship: the last line is the exact `held_cli.py ship --session <new>@<m>` to run next,
because `ship` needs `ghp`, which is absent on at least one fleet host. The resolution log under
`docs/decisions/resolutions/` is history and keeps the old slug.

**The landing pad.** `add` writes into `<destination repo>/.worktrees/<m>--<s>-agents/held-<s>` (the
board form of the session address) on branch `wt/<m>--<s>/held-<s>`, created at `origin/main` on first use (the leaf is `held-<s>`
because this bookkeeping has no Beads id of its own, and a leaf name must be unique per repo, so a
bare `held` let only the first session on a host create its pad, (internal ref); the creation guard
accepts the nested shape and refuses a flat one). It is never the ai-harness main tree and never another session's worktree. After every
squash merge `ship` resets it onto `origin/main`, so it is always one commit set ahead at most.
The session-boundary audit may reap it when it reads zero ahead and its owning session is not proved
live; while that session lives, every other caller's audit keeps it ((internal ref)). `add` recreates it.
The pad belongs to its SESSION, not to the process that created it ((internal ref)). Owner liveness
(`worktree_owner_liveness.py`) reads the pad's `aih-provenance.json`, not its branch stamp, so every
verb that touches a pad (and `migrate`, for the pad it moves or creates) rewrites that record's
`owner_session` to the pad's own session through `worktree_provenance.rebind_owner`, and, when the
calling process descends from that session, re-binds `owner_pid` and its process-start token to it.
A pad created for another session (the migrate hook) therefore names that session, and a relaunched
session's pad reads `ACTIVE` again on its first held verb. A missing or unreadable record is left
alone and named on stderr.

## What the chat says

**At emit time, by the owning session:** the body IS the chat output (the same text `add` was
given), followed by one line `Held: <absolute path>`. A decision's body already carries the three
lines of § Decisions are git-tracked before they are shown inside its block, so it is followed
only by the `**Open decision:**` block.

**As a pointer** (the chief, a `SendMessage`, a re-surface of an `answered` item): one line per
item, then the block `/format-decision` requires, nothing else:

```text
Held for you: /data/projects/ai-harness/docs/held/sem-kg-ec2--aih-2/2026-10-11-01-decision-xhc5u-d6-upgrade-claude-code.md
Ask: approve (a) upgrade now, or pick (b)/(c); one word is enough.

**Open decision:** D-6 upgrade route — recorded in /data/projects/ai-harness/docs/held/...
```

After a compaction, the owning session's `/auto-start` Step 4 replays its own `open` items in full
(§ Replay); another session's item is re-surfaced as that same path + ask + block, never its body.

## Who writes here

- **Every VP session**, at emit time for every output in the § Holding at emit time table, at
  `/exit-goal` Step 6 (one `exit-goal` index item for the report; each `/format-decision` +
  `/explain` pair is its own `decision` item, held by that skill's step), and whenever a decision
  or blocker must reach the repo owner mid-run.
- **The chief of staff**, for fleet-level escalations, the `/fleet-brief` it writes for the repo owner under
  its standing goal (`kind: fleet-brief`), and its own `/exit-goal` output.
- **Never** a sub-agent on its own: a leaf reports to its launcher, which decides what the repo owner must
  see, records it, holds it and compiles it.

Every writer is pointed here by the path-scoped rule `held-docs.md` (§ `/held-doc-review`), which
loads on any path under `docs/held/`.

Operating rules for the chief and VPs: [📄 ai-harness/docs/procedures/chief-of-staff-vp-coordination.md](../procedures/chief-of-staff-vp-coordination.md)
§ Held output for the repo owner.
